chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
It was (inscribed) upon the ring of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Disgraceful and wretched is the murderer of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)'.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (Title for Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What was inscribed on the ring of Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practice of engraving rings with specific titles or epithets, illustrating how the Ahl al-Bayt utilized personal adornment to preserve and proclaim key theological narratives. The inscription 'Disgraceful and wretched is the murderer of Al-Husayn' serves not only as a historical commemoration of Karbala but also as a perpetual declaration of the Imam's authority and the legitimacy of his lineage against their enemies. This practice underscores the Shia scholarly view that such inscriptions are acts of remembrance (dhikr) and a means of distinguishing the righteous from their adversaries in both spiritual and social contexts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was (inscribed) upon a ring of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> – ‘خَزِيَ وَ شَقِيَ قَاتِلُ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام )’ “Disgraceful and wretched is the murderer of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>”’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Afi ibn Ma’bad from af-Husayn ibn Khafid who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
On the ring of Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, the writing said, ‘Disgraced and destroyed are murderers of al-Husayn ibn Ah’ ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’”
